title: Smoothness↔split-prime is a provable ring-theoretic dichotomy (q≡1 mod 2^μ ⟺ μ_{2^μ} exists ⟺ 𝔮 fully splits) — structural ROOT of W-idealSVP
evidence: Two separable claims. (1) The CONGRUENCE DICHOTOMY is PROVEN (standard cyclotomic + cyclic-group theory) and machine-verified EXACTLY in the prize regime by scripts/probes/_407_conn/C068_split_dichotomy.py: for n=2^μ a proper subgroup, q prime ~n^β (β=4,5), across μ∈{3,4,5,6} and 4 split + 4 non-split primes each (q up to ~1.68e7), in EVERY instance: q≡1 mod n  ⟺  F_q* has an order-n (FFT) subgroup [n|q−1 on cyclic group of order q−1]  ⟺  q splits completely in ℚ(ζ_n), i.e. residue degree f=ord_n(q)=1, #primes above q = φ(n), N(𝔓)=q^f=q. Matched non-split side: q≢1 mod n ⟹ no FFT subgroup AND f=ord_n(q)>1 (residue degree >1, NOT fully split). All asserts pass; φ(n)=n/2 confirmed throughout. This is exactly the Dedekind/cyclotomic splitting law (f=ord of q in (ℤ/n)^×, full split ⟺ q≡1 mod n) plus F_q* cyclic ⟹ μ_n exists ⟺ n|q−1; both Mathlib-formalizable (isRoot_cyclotomic_iff, ZMod cyclic). So 'smoothness and the open fully-split (N(𝔮)=q, Pan-Xu) ideal-SVP class are governed by ONE congruence q≡1 mod 2^μ' is correct and rigorous. (2) The PRIZE-RELEVANT claim — that this dichotomy is the 'structural ROOT of why every face hits W-idealSVP' — is an obstruction-EXPLANATION, not a bound: it gives ZERO leverage on the BGK √-cancellation. It restates which prime class is hard; it does not estimate the representation mass Σ_z R_r(z) / max_b|η_b| that is the actual open core. The in-tree file CyclotomicNormDefectThreshold.lean carries the matching honest note: the norm threshold is VACUOUS in-regime (φ(n)=n/2 ⟹ p^{1/φ}→1), and the open wall (representation mass once (2r)^{φ(n)}≥p) is explicitly not addressed.
wall: W-idealSVP (equivalently W-BGK): the dichotomy localizes the prize regime to the fully-split / open Pan-Xu ideal-SVP class but the residual is unchanged — the high-r (r≈log q) equidistribution/representation-mass of the root-of-unity sumset mod 𝔭, the Bourgain–Shkredov thin-subgroup √-cancellation problem.
honest_note: PARTIAL, not a closure. What is proven (the congruence dichotomy with f=ord_n(q), full-split ⟺ q≡1 mod n, FFT ⟺ n|q−1) is standard textbook number theory — true, exactly machine-verified in the prize regime, and Lean-formalizable as the record's attack_plan states (smoothDomain_iff_fullySplit), but contributes NO progress on the open core. It is an explanatory mapping ('smoothness forces the open ideal-SVP class via one shared congruence') that welds straight back to W-idealSVP/W-BGK; it neither sharpens the open inequality (so NOT REDUCED) nor refutes anything. Honest value: a citable, formally-checkable obstruction explanation for why the prize regime coincides with the open Pan-Xu split class — already consistent with the campaign's W-idealSVP framing (RESEARCH_SYNTHESIS line 37: 'fully-split N(𝔮)=q open'). Probe uses exact integer arithmetic (sympy primality + multiplicative-order, no floats).
